about: Design-production status for the low-fidelity wireframes, and nothing else. It says which surface is in which review batch, which artefacts exist, in which language and viewport, which states they cover and how far the review has gone. It restates no requirement: the surface, its rows and its states are in design/inventory/surfaces.json, and every entry here points at one by its canonical id. Checked by tools/design_wireframes.py. The format and the workflow are in README.md and workflow.md beside this file.

review_statuses.briefed: A brief is generated. Nothing is drawn.
review_statuses.exploration: Being explored in the calibration set or in its batch. More than one treatment may exist.

directions.label: Clean Premium Commerce
directions.approach: Calm and restrained. Lower density, generous whitespace, a quiet header, large product imagery, and merchandising content used sparingly so the product carries each view.

directions.label: Editorial Modern Retail
directions.approach: Composed like a publication. Larger editorial blocks set among the products, strong typographic hierarchy, imagery that dominates, and grids that vary rather than repeat.

directions.label: Dynamic Contemporary Ecommerce
directions.approach: Energetic and efficient. Higher density, more products in view, prominent merchandising rails and badges, a utility-forward header, and the purchase actions kept close at hand.

directions_note: The labels are descriptive only. They are three structural approaches to hierarchy, density, composition and interaction, not three brand identities. All three satisfy the same scope, draw the same states, keep every pattern the contract fixes, and stay neutral. They may differ only in presentation and in interaction choices that are genuinely open. None adds a feature.

calibration.purpose: Establish the structural ecommerce direction on a representative set of first-release customer surfaces, in three directions, before it is carried across the inventory. Exploration: it locks nothing until the owner selects.

elements_from_other_directions.element: The one-page checkout structure, presented as Direction C's checkout, with a review section that restates the address, the shipping method, the payment method, the items and the full total before Place Order. A's shipping options are not taken: express delivery is SHIP-07, P2.
A single hero banner. The featured collections stay their own home section.
At most four products per row beside the desktop sidebar.
Quick add shown on hover and keyboard focus on desktop, and always visible on touch.
A mobile buy bar shown only after the in-page buy area leaves the view.

adaptations: A6 is not taken. The checkout keeps a condensed header with the logo, search, the language switcher, the account, the wishlist and the cart with its live count.

B1, Load More, is not selected. Numbered native pagination stays the provisional baseline of DQ-02, and Load More may be reconsidered as an enhancement of the native paged links at the high-fidelity review, on evidence.
Trending and new arrivals stay two separate home sections.
selection.decision_source: Mustafa, owner, 18 October 2026, on Claude Design's UX decision report and Claude Code's validation of the same date. A structural low-fidelity selection: not approval of the brand identity or of the interface design (PRE-03b), not a client confirmation, and no change to the contracted scope.

reconfirmation.record: A deliberate review and approval of the final structural UX direction, after the selection above was first recorded in #353 (c139c45). The selection stands, and the fields above are kept as first recorded. Direction C is the structural baseline, with premium A-inspired restraint applied consistently across the full storefront. Not approval of the brand colours, the typography, the imagery, the high-fidelity interface or PRE-03b, not a client confirmation, and no change to the contracted scope.
reconfirmation.kept_from_c: The contemporary navigation, search, product discovery and filtering, the product detail architecture, the sticky desktop purchase area, the cart, the mini-cart and the checkout presentation.
reconfirmation.applied_throughout: Calmer hierarchy, purposeful whitespace, reduced visual clutter, restrained card treatment and product-led composition, on every storefront surface.
refinements: IX-02 is refined: a deliberate click or tap of the cart control opens the drawer, with focus managed and returned to the control that opened it; a successful quick add from a listing or a product rail is confirmed in place, updates the header count and is announced, without opening the drawer or moving focus away from the quick add; a failed add shows its error, with no success message and no change to the count; an add from the cart's suggestions does not automatically open another drawer. The confirmation after Add to Cart on the product page is IX-10, open for the batch-03 review: the owner allows the drawer there and has not chosen it.

IX-08 stands as recorded: the full description stays a tab (PDP-12), the key features and the purchase information are reachable without opening several tabs, and delivery, returns and authenticity are clearly reachable.

IX-09 stands: one prominent hero, never an autoplaying carousel. Category shortcuts (HOME-05) and the featured collections (HOME-04) are separate sections, and trending (HOME-02) and new arrivals (HOME-03) are separate, independently managed sections. Purposeful motion is allowed where it never obstructs shopping or costs performance.

The checkout stands: DQ-03's one page with C's presentation, every required review item before Place Order, the condensed header with the logo, search, account, wishlist, cart and language switcher, and no express delivery in the first release (SHIP-07, P2).
DQ-01 and DQ-02 stay provisional: Western digits and native numbered pagination are the working baselines, and Load More is not newly authorised.

Motion: purposeful microinteractions, accessible overlays and meaningful feedback; no compulsory carousel motion, no scroll-jacking and no animation that delays a purchase; reduced motion and mobile performance are design constraints. A Lighthouse score of 99 to 100 is an aspirational engineering target, not a contractual guarantee.

Account, batches 04 and 06: a coherent desktop sidebar and mobile account navigation, a dashboard with recent orders and their statuses, clear profile and password sections, and accurate verification, cart-merge, recovery and account-security states. The account audit and its signed-scope validation are planning references, not authority to change the inventoried states; the account's technical and scope decisions stay with those batch reviews and do not block batch-01.

decisions.decision: Numbered pagination for first-release product listings and search results, with addressable pages, keyboard accessibility, page order following the reading direction in Arabic and a predictable return to the same place in the list. Locked in interaction-options.json. Load More and infinite scrolling are not added as launch functionality.

At most one primary merchandising badge per product card, in this order: Limited, then New, then Best Seller, then Trending. The sale saving may appear separately where it applies. No new merchandising capability, admin field, artificial urgency or unsupported marketing claim.

accepted: The single-panel mobile filter drawer with collapsible groups (IX-01).
The variable-product quick add as a small non-modal panel anchored to the card, keeping IX-02 and the documented focus, Escape and announcement behaviour (US-03-01).
The Arabic pagination presentation: the sequence follows the reading direction, previous and next mirror, digits do not.
The routine interpretations: no explicit in-stock line on a card (PLP-03, wording PRE-09), no Brand filter on a brand page (PLP-07), and loading_more and end_of_list drawn for numbered pages.
